text:

I noticed there is not much activity on this subforum but hopefully will get a few responses.

LDN and Glutamate. I started LDN because I thought it would help decrease levels of glutamate in my brain.  It is widely reported that LDN inhibits glial cells which produce glutamate on LDN pages.
Like this one:
http://www.ldnresearchtrust.org/node/188
However, LDN increases levels of beta endorphins drastically...which have been shown to enhance glutamate neurotoxicity in the hypothalamus by disrupting the calcium balance.
http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/m/pubmed/11938958/?i=2&from=/10374630/related
How can both of these things be true?  Any ideas?

text:
Wide variety of experiences with LDN, as with most treatments for ME.  One person says it takes several weeks to kick in; for me it kicked in overnight.  Someone feels that consistent dosing is important; I tried several widely different doses, with minimal change in effect.  For some people, it reduces general ME symptoms; for me it blocked ME-generated pain, but did so 100%, but had no effect on other ME symptoms.  You won't know what effects it will (or won't) have, or what dosing is best, without experimenting.
I found dosing of LDN to be important over a small range.  2.0 mg had no effect

According to the research I've read and anecdotal evidence from patients, including myself, LDN is an immune system modulater. It can up or down regulate your immune system, depending on what your body needs. Some of the best evidence for this includes several studies on MS sufferers and HIV, where it has stopped the progression of the illness, and in some cases, reversed it.
Many users, as reported in the LDN thread on this forum, have experienced immune responses after starting LDN.
